Source: the Recorder of Deeds fee schedule published on the county website. An easement or right of way costs $59.75, and a power of attorney used to sell real estate costs $18.50 plus parcel certification.

Smaller lines round out the schedule. A Statement of Value costs $2 and counts toward the page total, certifications cost $2.50, and copies are fifty cents a page.

How should a closing agent pay the Northampton County recorder?

Make payment out to "Recorder of Deeds." Personal checks are refused. Business checks, certified checks, money orders and cash all work, and a single check can cover five documents at most.

The exact amount has to accompany each document, and the office turns away overpayments. Closing packages built on a rough guess run into that rule, so build the number line by line from the schedule above.

  • Count the pages first, then add the $2 for every page past four.
  • Add $10 for each parcel on documents marked with an asterisk on the schedule.
  • Count names past four at $0.50 each.
  • Add the separate transfer tax payment if the deed is taxable.

Which paper rules does the Easton recorder enforce?

The schedule opens with its house rules, and they decide whether a deed is recorded or returned.

  • Parcel numbers must appear on every document that relates to real estate. The county points filers to its public parcel search at ncpub.org.
  • Pages are meant to be letter size, 8.5 by 11 inches. A paper that cannot comply, with 8.5 by 14 as the only allowed exception, pays a $10 penalty.
  • Blanket assignments, releases and satisfaction pieces are refused.
  • Anything coming back by mail needs a return envelope with the right postage already on it.

Not every filing is a deed. If a sale involves a new lot line or survey, the county charges $35 for the first page of a subdivision, site or survey plan and $30 for each added page. State highway plans cost $15 for the first page and $3 after that, and a lease for 30 years or longer costs $59.75. Full-size map copies up to 36 by 48 inches are $25.

The county also states that every document is microfilmed and open to public inspection, so what gets filed in Easton becomes searchable by anyone. The page count matters because the fee is built on it. A deed with a long legal description and an attached exhibit can pass four pages quickly, so check before you assume the base price.

How does transfer tax work on a Northampton County sale?

On a taxable deed the recorder takes the state's 1 percent along with whatever local transfer tax the municipality and school district impose. State rules hold the grantor and the grantee jointly responsible.

The state exempts some deeds, among them certain family transfers, deeds to a government body and inherited property. If you believe your deed fits, tell the title agent early. For the local share, call the recorder's office and give the municipality where the house stands, because the figure can differ from one borough or township to the next.

Who actually pays is a matter for the sales contract, so read that clause before closing.

What is the Northampton County housing picture for sellers?

Easton is the seat and Bethlehem the biggest city of this Lehigh Valley county. Carved from Bucks County in 1752, it spans 377 square miles, with the Delaware River along its eastern edge and the Lehigh River cutting through.

Heavy industry shaped it. Bethlehem Steel was based in Bethlehem until it was dissolved in 2003, and the region also made cement. The Census Bureau estimated 324,411 residents in 2025.

Housing costs sit well below Montgomery County to the south. The latest five-year survey shows a $308,600 median home, $89,184 median household income and owners in 71.1 percent of occupied units. The county adopted a home rule charter in 1978, with a county executive and a council.

Which Northampton County municipalities send deeds to this office?

All of them. Two cities, Bethlehem and Easton, sit among many boroughs and townships, yet every deed for land inside the county line is recorded in the same Easton office.

The largest places by the 2010 census were Bethlehem at 74,982 people, a city that spills partly into Lehigh County, then Easton at 26,800, Bethlehem Township at 23,730, Palmer Township at 20,691 and Forks Township at 14,721. Smaller boroughs include Northampton, Wilson, Hellertown, Nazareth, Bangor, Pen Argyl and Wind Gap.

Two points follow for a seller. Part of Bethlehem lies in Lehigh County, a different county with its own recorder, so confirm which side your house is on before planning the closing. And local transfer tax and school district bills follow the municipality, so a sale in Hellertown can price out differently from one in Palmer Township.

What should I check before closing a Northampton County sale?

Most delays are paper problems, not legal ones. Work through the list a few days ahead.

  • Confirm the parcel number on the deed matches the county's parcel search.
  • Count pages and names to get the exact fee, with no overpayment.
  • Ask whether the title company will deliver by 4:00 p.m., since parcel-certified recordings close early.
  • Pull the tax certification and any unpaid tax before the closing date.
  • Ask the title agent how the Statement of Value is being counted in the page total.
  • Collect a return envelope with correct postage if the deed is coming back by mail.

Open mortgage balances get released through a satisfaction piece, which costs $61.75 to record. Ask the lender how long it takes to file one so the buyer's title is clean.

More questions about Northampton County, PA Recorder of Deeds

What will it run me to file a deed in Easton?

Plan on $76.25 for a deed of four pages and four names. Add $10 per certified parcel, $2 for each extra page and 50 cents for each extra name.

Can I pay the Northampton County recorder with a personal check?

No. The county takes business checks, certified checks, money orders and cash, and caps a check at five documents.

Can I overpay the recording fee in Northampton County?

No. The office wants the exact fee with each document and refuses overpayments, so work out the total before the package goes out.

When does the Northampton County recorder stop taking documents?

The counter stays open until 4:30 p.m., but anything needing a parcel certification must be in by 4:00 p.m. A later deed waits for the next business day.

Who pays the transfer tax on a Northampton County sale?

State law makes both sides jointly responsible for the 1 percent state tax. The contract decides who actually pays, so check that clause.

Luzerne County by the numbers

Where does Luzerne County record deeds, and what are the hours?

Luzerne County deeds are recorded in Wilkes-Barre by the Recorder of Deeds, whose public counter is in the Courthouse Annex at 153 N. River Street. Mail goes to 200 N. River Street, Wilkes-Barre, PA 18711, and the phone number is 570-825-1641. The counter is open Monday through Friday from 9:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., closed on holidays, and the filing cutoff is 4:20 p.m.

A second counter in Hazleton operates only on Tuesdays and Thursdays from 10:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. That office takes no cash. It accepts money orders, cashier's checks, personal and business checks, and credit cards, and the customer must wait while staff complete the documents. Electronic recording can be submitted at any hour.

The same annex houses the Assessors' Office, which matters because every deed needs a parcel number certified before it can be recorded.

What does it cost to record a deed in Luzerne County?

The fee schedule effective November 17, 2025 sets the base charge for a deed or a mortgage at $72.75. That covers up to four pages, four names and one PIN. Luzerne County then added a $15.00 charge to deeds, exempt deeds and mortgages starting July 1, 2026, to fund a county demolition program for blighted buildings. Adding the two gives $87.75, but ask the office to confirm the total for your document.

Luzerne County recording fees, base amounts on the schedule effective November 17, 2025 (source: Luzerne County Recorder of Deeds fee schedule)
DocumentBase fee
Deed$72.75
Mortgage$72.75
Satisfaction$64.75
Release of mortgage$64.75
Assignment of mortgage$64.75
Deed easement or right of way$64.75
Timber conveyance$33.50
Power of attorney$23.50

Smaller charges to watch for:

  • Each page over four costs $2.00, and each name over four costs $0.50.
  • Each PIN after the first costs $0.50 at the Recorder, while the Assessor's Office bills its own fee to certify each PIN. Call 570-825-1525 for the current amount.
  • A rejected document costs $10.00 by mail and $5.00 when sent electronically.
  • A returned check costs $35.00.
  • The office will not take more than 10 documents on a single check and does not refund an overpayment. It will return the check for a corrected one or keep the overage.

How much transfer tax do Luzerne County buyers and sellers pay?

The state charges 1 percent, and the county schedule gives the combined rate by municipality. The county's schedule says the total is 2 percent in all municipalities except three: Wilkes-Barre at 3.5 percent, Pittston at 3.5 percent and Kingston Borough at 2.5 percent. It also lists Hazleton at a 2 percent total. With 76 municipalities in the county, the rate that applies to your house depends on the address, so check which borough, city or township you are in before you work out proceeds.

The Pennsylvania Department of Revenue says both grantor and grantee are jointly and severally liable for the tax, and that certain family transfers, transfers by will or intestacy, and transfers to government units are exempt. For a deed claiming an exemption, the county asks that the document say why, for example parent and child, and a non-family exemption needs a Statement of Value.

A property that spans two municipalities must state in the deed the percentage that lies in each, because the local portion is divided between them.

What does the recorder need on a Luzerne County deed?

Every deed, mortgage and assignment must carry a PIN certified by the Assessor's Office and a signed, certified address for the grantee or mortgagee. Ask the Assessor to certify the number in the top margin, and leave a 2 1/2 inch blank margin at the bottom of at least two pages so the recording stamps fit.

  • Statement of Value (REV-183): one original and one copy, completed with the school district, assessed value and common level ratio, and signed and dated by a person connected to the transaction. It counts as a page, and any attached exhibits also count at $2.00 a page.
  • Numbering: when several documents make up one transaction, number them in the order they should be recorded. If the presenter submits them in the wrong order, the presenter pays for re-recording.
  • Self-addressed stamped envelopes for the return of documents and receipts.
  • Non-standard financing forms are not accepted, and blanket assignments and blanket releases are refused.

The office posts common level ratios effective July 1 of 2024, 2025 and 2026 among its related documents, so use the one in effect on the date of the transfer.

How do I search Luzerne County land records?

The recorder's office offers three online routes. Landex Remote is a prepaid account that draws down as you view records, covering images from 1968 to the present with indexing from December 1980. Landex Webstore lets you search the indices for free and charges a fee for each document you view or print. IQS Infodex, at searchiqs.com/paluze, is free to search for older deeds from 1786 to 1967, and it also holds grantor and grantee indices from 1786 to August 1, 1993.

Certified copies are available only in the office. A plain copy by mail costs $5.00 for the first page and $2.00 for each added page. Staff cannot run title searches for individuals and cannot give legal or tax advice, so title work stays with an attorney or title company.

Owners can also sign up for the county's free Record Alert service through Landex, which watches up to five PINs or names and emails the owner when a document is recorded. It does not stop a filing, because the office must record any properly executed document with payment, but it gives an owner an early warning about a fraudulent deed.

What should a seller know about Luzerne County?

Luzerne County was formed on September 25, 1786 from Northumberland County, and it once covered much of the northeast before Bradford, Lackawanna, Susquehanna and Wyoming counties were cut from it. Today it covers 906 square miles, is a home rule county, and holds 76 municipalities, more than any county except Allegheny. The 2020 census counted 325,594 residents, and the 2025 estimate is 332,126. The county's population peaked at 445,109 in 1930 during the anthracite boom.

  • Cities: Wilkes-Barre (44,328 in 2020), Hazleton (29,963), Nanticoke (10,628) and Pittston (7,591), plus larger boroughs such as Kingston (13,349).
  • School districts: Wilkes-Barre Area, Hazleton Area, Wyoming Valley West, Pittston Area, Dallas, Crestwood, Greater Nanticoke Area, Hanover Area, Lake-Lehman, Northwest Area, Wyoming Area and Berwick Area.
  • Roads and travel: Interstates 80, 81 and 476, US 11, and the Wilkes-Barre/Scranton International Airport.
  • Work: warehousing and logistics have replaced much of the old manufacturing, alongside healthcare, higher education and energy generation.

The Susquehanna River runs through the Wyoming Valley, and land elevation ranges from about 512 feet to 2,460 feet, so homes sit in very different settings from river flats to mountain ridges. Verify the municipality and school district on the tax bill, because both change the transfer tax and the yearly tax.

More questions about Luzerne County, PA Recorder of Deeds

How much is the base fee to record a deed in Luzerne County?

The base fee is $72.75 on the schedule effective November 17, 2025, with $15.00 added from July 1, 2026 for the county demolition fund. The office can confirm the current total.

What is the realty transfer tax rate in Luzerne County?

The county lists a 2 percent total in most municipalities. Wilkes-Barre and Pittston are 3.5 percent, and Kingston Borough is 2.5 percent.

Can I pay for Luzerne County recording with cash?

The Hazleton counter takes no cash, and the schedule lists checks, money orders and cashier's checks. Ask the Wilkes-Barre counter before you bring cash there.

Does Luzerne County require a Statement of Value?

A Statement of Value is required when a deed claims a non-family exemption. File one original and one copy, completed, signed and dated.

How can I find an old Luzerne County deed?

Search Landex for records from 1968 forward, or the free IQS Infodex site for deeds from 1786 to 1967. Certified copies must be requested at the office in person.

Lackawanna County by the numbers

Where is the Lackawanna County Recorder of Deeds, and when can I record a deed?

The office sits at 123 Wyoming Avenue, Suite 218, in Scranton, and the number is 570-963-6775. Hours run from 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., but the counter stops taking documents for recording at 3:45 p.m.

A signed deed can reach the office three ways: carried in, dropped in the box in the main lobby of the Government Center, or sent by U.S. Mail. Title companies often skip all three and file electronically through Simplifile, CSC or ePN, the vendors the county lists on its Recorder of Deeds page.

The Recorder records and indexes property documents, and it also collects realty transfer tax for the state, the municipality and the school district. Anyone selling a house in Lackawanna County meets this office on the last day of the sale, after the deed has been signed and notarized at closing.

What must a Lackawanna County deed contain before it is recorded?

It has to meet the county's written recording requirements, which have followed national PRIA document standards since September 1, 2024. Missing items are the usual reason a closing package gets sent back.

  • Paper size of 8.5 by 11 inches (8.5 by 14 is tolerated), type no smaller than 12 point, and margins of at least one inch on every page.
  • Original signatures in dark ink. Handwriting is not allowed anywhere else on the page, and highlighter marks are not allowed at all.
  • A complete legal description naming the municipality, county and state, plus the county tax parcel number. The Assessment Office certifies each parcel number before the deed is recorded, and mailed packages are forwarded there first.
  • A formal acknowledgment before a notary or another authorized officer, showing the date, the signer's name, the notary's signature and the expiration date.
  • A Certificate of Residence signed by the buyer, giving a precise address.
  • Written dollar amounts that match the numbers, since consideration is checked against the transfer tax paid.

A deed cannot be fixed by re-recording it. Errors are corrected with a Corrective Deed, which must carry a Statement of Value, an explanation, and a full copy of the deed being corrected.

How do I pay the Lackawanna County Recorder, and what happens with an overpayment?

Pay by check for the exact amount. The office's requirements sheet says it does not accept credit cards and does not refund overages, and it asks that the submitter's address be printed on every check.

Payment rules in the Lackawanna County recording requirements sheet (revised August 2024)

Overpayment above $5.00Document is returned
Returned check$20.00 fee

Make checks payable to the Lackawanna County Recorder of Deeds. A check whose memo line points to some other land document is refused, and the office may ask for ID to confirm the address on a check.

Base recording amounts depend on page, name and parcel counts. The county posts a fee calculator on its Recorder page, so run the deed through it, or call before you write the check.

How is realty transfer tax handled on a Lackawanna County sale?

The Recorder collects it when the deed is recorded. Pennsylvania sets the state rate at 1 percent of the value, and the Department of Revenue makes buyer and seller jointly responsible for it. Local shares go to the municipality and school district on top of that.

Some transfers escape the tax, including certain family transfers and property passing by will or intestacy. Even then the Recorder wants the exemption stated in the deed or on a fully completed Statement of Value.

  • When land lies in more than one municipality, the deed must give each municipality's percentage and dollar amount in whole numbers, backed by a Statement of Value.
  • A deed that recites the wrong location is the submitter's problem: the right tax must be paid to the right municipality, and the refund from the wrong one has to be chased by the submitter.
  • Easements also need a Statement of Value, and it counts toward the page total.

What changed in Lackawanna County recording fees in late 2025 and 2026?

Two things. A state budget change signed on November 12, 2025 raised the court-related surcharge on every recording, so the combined court and AOPC portion went from $40.25 to $41.25. The Recorder began collecting the higher amount on November 17, 2025, and packages mailed in with the old amount were sent back to be redone.

Second, since January 1, 2026, attachments on e-recorded documents, such as a Corrective Deed or Deed of Trust, cost an extra $0.50 per page, because the office must print them for the Department of Revenue. Documents brought in, dropped off or mailed do not pick up that per-page charge.

Anyone who prepares a closing package from an older checklist should ask the office for the current total before sending a check.

How did the Lackawanna County reassessment change things for sellers?

The county finished its first full reassessment in nearly 60 years in 2025, moving values off 1968 levels to current market values. A court ordered it after a 2022 resident lawsuit, and the Assessment Office says the county millage rate fell from 89.98 to 5.79 mills to keep the change revenue-neutral.

The county describes the result as roughly a third of owners paying more, a third paying less and a third about the same. A quarterly payment option was introduced for property tax bills. For a seller, the practical point is that an old tax bill says little about what a buyer will pay, so pull the current assessment record before you list.

The appeal deadline for 2027 consideration was August 1, 2026, and the county says appeals open again on April 1, 2027. The Clean & Green application window for 2027 closed June 1, 2026, with the next one starting March 1, 2027. The county also posts a form under Act 29 of 2026 for owners of rentals, LLCs, trusts and other entity-held property bought on or after September 18, 2026.

What is Lackawanna County like for someone selling a house?

Lackawanna County covers 465 square miles in northeastern Pennsylvania, with Scranton as county seat and Carbondale as the other city. It was created on August 13, 1878, the last Pennsylvania county formed, and it grew around anthracite mining and iron and steel. I-81, I-84, I-380 and I-476 all cross it. Twelve public school districts serve it, from Abington Heights and Dunmore to Scranton and North Pocono.

Lackawanna County housing figures, Census Bureau QuickFacts

Population estimate, July 2025216,502
Housing units, July 2025100,686
Owner-occupied rate, 2020-202465.4%
Median owner-occupied home value, 2020-2024$201,800
Median gross rent, 2020-2024$1,007
Median household income, 2020-2024$66,223

Winters are cold: downtown Scranton averages 26.0 degrees in January and 71.9 in July. Plan for snow-season showings and for heating costs when you price a vacant house.

What should I have in hand at a Lackawanna County closing?

A short list heads off most rejections at the counter.

  • The deed, signed in original ink and acknowledged, with the notary stamp clear and nothing typed or written onto it.
  • The county tax parcel number and a full legal description.
  • A signed Certificate of Residence from the buyer.
  • A completed Statement of Value if any tax is excused or the price is not shown on the deed.
  • A check for the exact total, with the submitter's address printed on it.
  • A self-addressed stamped envelope if you want the recorded original mailed back.

Deliver it before 3:45 p.m. on a business day, or have the title company file it electronically.

More questions about Lackawanna County, PA Recorder of Deeds

Can I pay for recording in Lackawanna County with a credit card?

No, according to the office's requirements sheet, which says it does not accept credit cards. Bring a check for the exact amount, made out to the Lackawanna County Recorder of Deeds. A single check may cover both the recording fee and the transfer tax.

What time does Lackawanna County stop recording deeds?

Recording ends at 3:45 p.m. The office stays open until 4:00 p.m., and it opens at 9:00 a.m. A deed that arrives after 3:45 waits for the next business day.

Does a Lackawanna County deed need a parcel number?

Yes. Every document that relates directly to real estate must carry the county tax parcel number, and the Assessment Office certifies it before recording. A mailed package is forwarded to that office for the certification first.

Can a mistake in a recorded deed be fixed by recording it again?

No. The office says deeds can only be corrected with a Corrective Deed. It must include a Statement of Value, a reason for the correction, and a complete copy of the deed being corrected.

Who pays realty transfer tax when a Lackawanna County house sells?

Under Department of Revenue rules, buyer and seller are both liable for the state 1 percent tax. Your sales contract can say who actually pays. The Recorder collects it with the deed and passes it on to the state, the municipality and the school district.

Dauphin County by the numbers

Where is the Dauphin County Recorder of Deeds office?

The office is in the Dauphin County Courthouse, Room 102, at 101 Market Street in Harrisburg. Staff are there weekdays until half past four, starting at eight, and the number to call is (717) 780-6560.

Everything filed against Dauphin County land passes through this counter or its online equivalent: deeds, mortgages, satisfactions, easements, plans and powers of attorney. The office describes its job narrowly. It records, reproduces and indexes documents that the law allows to be recorded, and it does not give title advice.

A seller who works with a title company will rarely deal with the office directly. The settlement agent prepares the deed, adds the fees and transfer tax, and sends it in.

What does the Dauphin County recorder charge for recording?

Deeds and mortgages each carry an $87.75 fee on the schedule revised December 1, 2025. The schedule says that any document needing a Unified Parcel Identifier adds $20.00 for each identifier, so a one parcel deed totals $107.75.

Dauphin County Recorder of Deeds price sheet, revised December 1, 2025

Source: the Dauphin County Recorder of Deeds schedule of fees. A page beyond the fourth costs $2.00, and a name beyond the ninth costs fifty cents. Most simple instruments such as affidavits, agreements, releases and notices are $18.50.

The office says these fees come from the Commonwealth through the General Assembly and can change over time. A fee calculator on the office web page works out the total for a given document.

How is transfer tax split on a Dauphin County sale?

Per the county FAQ, a 2% levy applies to what is paid for the property. One point belongs to the Department of Revenue, with a half point apiece for the township or borough and the school district.

The state's revenue page adds that both parties to a deed answer for the state's share together, and that the recorder forwards it. The purchase agreement is where a buyer and seller decide who pays.

  • The FAQ lists conveyances between spouses, parents and children, grandparents and grandchildren, and brothers and sisters as exempt, and other exemptions exist in special cases.
  • A deed for nominal consideration, such as $1, between tax exempt parties carries $0 of transfer tax and does not need separate checks.
  • State law also exempts property passed by will or by intestate succession, along with burial site deeds and certain transfers to governments.

A $230,000 sale would carry $4,600 at that rate. Have the settlement agent confirm the final figure before closing.

How are fees paid, and when do originals return?

Cash and checks are the accepted ways to pay, and checks name the Dauphin County Recorder of Deeds. Anything mailed in needs a stamped return envelope with your address on it, plus the correct amount.

In most cases the original goes back to the person who presented it within a day or two, although busy periods, holidays and staffing can stretch that. If two weeks pass with nothing in hand, the FAQ tells you to ask the firm that filed it.

Large closings often go through a title company, so ask which firm will submit the deed and how it will pay the fees.

How far back do Dauphin County records go?

The first recorded registry dates to 1785. The office website holds deeds and miscellaneous documents from 1785 forward and mortgages from 1979 forward, and it has the deed indexes and a mortgage index online under the Alpha Index.

The FAQ explains the handling of the originals. Each document is scanned and the original is kept until the indexes and records are checked and proofed by at least two people. Images are backed up to hard drive and microfilmed to meet the Pennsylvania Historical Museum Commission requirements, and the microfilm is stored off-site in an underground facility so records can be recreated after a courthouse disaster.

Nearly everything recorded is public. The exception is a military discharge paper, DD214. Search access requires accepting the office's disclaimer, which states that the official records are those held in the office.

What else does the Dauphin County recorder handle besides deeds?

Notaries start here. A new notary brings identification, the completed notary bond and payment, and the office records the bond and commission and administers the oath. The notary then walks to the Prothonotary to register a signature. The FAQ says no appointment is needed, and the filing fee is $33.50 on the schedule.

The office also takes plans at $20.50 for the first page and $5.00 for each page after, and it files Uniform Commercial Code statements at $100.00. Certified copies cost $2.00 plus the per page copy charge, microfilm copies are $0.75 and photocopies are $0.50 a page.

One misunderstanding comes up with burial plots. A cemetery lot deed normally grants permission to use the ground, while the cemetery keeps title, and those papers are held by the cemetery company or association, not by the county.

What common questions come up before a Dauphin County sale?

Several questions repeat at the counter, and the FAQ answers them directly.

  • A change of ownership needs a new deed prepared and recorded. Merely stating a change does nothing.
  • After a mortgage is paid, the lender typically sends a satisfaction to the office. The owner does not get a new deed.
  • If a spouse dies and the couple held title as tenants by the entirety, the survivor generally explains the death in the next deed or mortgage. Other forms of title, such as tenants in common, may need different handling, and the office suggests asking an attorney.
  • A deed for a lot usually covers buildings erected on it, now or later.
  • A deed gives a legal description of boundaries, but a surveyor places markers on the ground.

Anyone can write their own deed, though the office recommends having an attorney prepare it so the recording criteria are met and the right fee is enclosed.

What do the Census numbers say about Dauphin County?

The Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 293,351 people, up from 286,401 in the 2020 count. The county spans 524.87 square miles, which works out to about 545.7 residents per square mile, and it holds 129,660 housing units.

For 2020 to 2024, QuickFacts reports a middle home value of $236,400 among owners, who occupy 63.1% of homes. Renters pay $1,217 in the middle of the range, and the middle household earns $76,242. Permits issued in 2025 numbered 329, and a commute averages 21.5 minutes.

Compared with the neighboring counties on the same table, Dauphin has the lowest median home value and the lowest owner occupancy.

More questions about Dauphin County, PA Recorder of Deeds

What will a Dauphin County deed cost to record?

The deed fee is $87.75 on the December 1, 2025 revision, with $20.00 added for each Unified Parcel Identifier and $2.00 for every page after the fourth. Transfer tax is figured separately from the sale price.

What transfer tax rate applies in Dauphin County?

The county FAQ gives 2% of the value conveyed, divided as 1% for the state and a half percent each for the municipality and school district. Some transfers between close relatives are exempt.

Does the Recorder of Deeds accept cards?

The county FAQ lists cash and check as accepted payment for recording fees. Make checks payable to Dauphin County Recorder of Deeds. Ask the office by phone before relying on any other method.

When does a recorded deed come back to me?

Within one to two days in most cases, according to the office, though volume, holidays and staffing can add time. After two weeks without your papers, contact whoever submitted them.

Can I search Dauphin County deeds online?

Yes. The office website has deeds and miscellaneous documents from 1785 and mortgages from 1979, searchable after you accept a disclaimer. Military discharge papers are the one category not open to the public.

What we confirmed on the official page

  • Deed and mortgage fee $104.75 first 4 pages (eff. Nov 17, 2025); $2/page over 4; $0.50/name over 4; Statement of Value $1.00; includes $20 UPI fee if required.

What we could not confirm

  • Judicial sale timeline not found
  • County upset sale/eRecording pages did not render

Cumberland County by the numbers

Where do I take a Cumberland County deed for recording?

The Recorder of Deeds works out of the Historic Courthouse at One Courthouse Square in Carlisle. Every deed, mortgage and related paper for land in the county's boroughs and townships lands in its index.

The counter opens on weekdays, with an occasional remote day, and closes at four in the afternoon. Because of that, the office wants visitors to book an appointment first. Notaries and anyone filing a subdivision plan must have one. Call 717.240.6370 or email recorder@cumberlandcountypa.gov to set a time.

Most sellers never go. The closing agent drafts the deed, collects the money and sends the package in on the seller's behalf.

What is the price of recording a deed in Cumberland?

Recording a deed runs $104.75 on the price list dated November 17, 2025. That figure folds in the $20 parcel identifier charge where one is needed, and every parcel beyond the first adds another $20.

Cumberland County Recorder of Deeds price list dated November 17, 2025
DocumentFee
Deed$104.75
Mortgage$104.75
Satisfaction piece$78.25
Assignment of mortgage$78.25
Agreement of sale$78.25
Power of attorney with a parcel number$37.00
Notary public$34.00
Subdivision plan$47.00

Source: the Cumberland County Recorder of Deeds fee schedule. Past the fourth page, each sheet adds $2.00, and a name beyond the fourth adds fifty cents. A Statement of Value costs $1.00 more.

A one dollar increase in the Criminal Justice Enhancement Account charge under Act 45 of 2025 is why deed and mortgage prices rose on that date. Per the county FAQ, Harrisburg sets most amounts, while the parcel identifier fee comes from a county ordinance.

How is realty transfer tax collected on a Cumberland County sale?

The Recorder takes the tax at the counter when a taxable deed arrives. The county's FAQ describes the full burden as 2% of the price: one point to the Commonwealth, and the other point shared equally by the municipality and the school district. Money moves to those bodies at month end, and the county keeps 1% of the state's portion and 2% of the local portion as a commission.

  • Under state law the grantor and grantee answer jointly for the tax, which makes the sale contract the place to assign it.
  • Some family transfers and property passing by will or intestacy are exempt. Staff do not rule on exemptions, so ask a lawyer or the Revenue Department.
  • The Statement of Value, form REV-183, goes with the deed when an exemption is claimed, when the real consideration differs from the figure on the deed's face, or when the deed is over 30 days old.

A $310,000 house sale produces $6,200 in combined transfer tax before recording fees.

Does Cumberland County take electronic recordings?

Yes, through three vendors only: ePN, CSC and Simplifile. The county says attorneys and title companies file most documents this way.

Paper still works. A mailed deed needs original signatures and notary stamps, since a photocopy cannot be recorded. If the check or card amount is wrong, the package comes back unfiled, unless the overage is $10 or less, in which case the office keeps the difference and records the paper.

Write checks to Recorder of Deeds. Cards go through Value Payment Systems with a 2.25% charge, a $2.50 floor, and 3% on business cards. Cash refunds are not given.

How old are the deed books held in Cumberland County?

The office has kept a continuous record since 1750, so a title search can reach deeds from the colonial period. Its history page says the books came through the courthouse fire of 1845 unscathed and were hidden away during the Confederate invasion of 1863.

Until 1929 every instrument was copied by hand into canvas bound volumes. Typed books followed, with separate indexes for deeds, mortgages and miscellaneous papers until December 1993, when the index was computerized. Paper books ended in 2001, and the old volumes moved from the courthouse to the County Archives in November 2017.

Landex lets anyone search back to 1750 around the clock, and the office has public computers for the same job. Searches run by name rather than address. To learn who owns a given parcel, ask the Tax Assessment Office or use the county's GIS Property Mapper.

What should a Cumberland County seller check around recording?

Clear every lien before closing, because the Recorder only holds mortgages and secured transactions. The county FAQ says judgment liens, municipal liens and state tax liens are filed with the Prothonotary, so a title search should cover both offices.

  • A lender records a satisfaction piece when a mortgage is paid. The homeowner receives no new deed.
  • Staff are neither bonded nor allowed to search title or advise on law. Hire a title searcher, an abstract company or an attorney.
  • Plans from the early 1900s onward may be on file, and the deed's property description often cites a plan book and page.
  • A veteran can record a DD214, and a certified copy is free should the original be lost. Discharge papers stay closed to public view.

For properties that reach the Tax Claim Bureau's online upset sale, the 2026 sale terms add transfer tax and recording fees on top of the winning bid. The tax is the assessed value, times the Common Level Ratio Factor, times 2%.

The county's upset sale Q&A says there is no redemption period once a sale closes. An owner may still file objections or exceptions with the local court up to thirty days after the court's confirmation nisi of the consolidated return. The 2026 continued sale was held online through Bid4Assets on October 23, and an owner with back tax should call the Tax Claim Bureau at 717-240-6367 before any listing goes live.

What is the Cumberland County housing picture for a seller?

Census Bureau figures for the county show 277,270 people in the July 2025 estimate, 6.9% more than the 2020 base, living on 545.48 square miles. In 2020 that worked out to 475.7 people for each square mile.

QuickFacts counts 114,465 housing units. Owners live in 71.3% of occupied homes, and the middle owner occupied value is $277,600 for 2020 to 2024. A typical household brings in $87,494, and typical gross rent is $1,249. Permits for 745 buildings were issued in 2025.

The 2026 county rate is 2.875 mills, with municipal and school rates added. Totals on the county's sheet run from about 15.95 mills in Hampden Township to about 27.27 mills in Newville Borough, so where the house sits matters a lot for the annual bill.

More questions about Cumberland County, PA Recorder of Deeds

What does Cumberland charge for a deed recording?

The charge is $104.75 on the price list dated November 17, 2025, with the $20 parcel identifier fee included where required. Pages past four are $2.00 each and names past four are fifty cents each. Transfer tax is paid on top.

Which party owes the transfer tax on a Cumberland County sale?

Both do, as far as the state is concerned: grantor and grantee answer jointly. Who actually pays is a matter for the sale contract. The tax totals 2% and is collected when the deed is recorded.

Will the Recorder of Deeds research my title?

No. The staff may not conduct title searches or give legal advice, though they can show you how to use the public terminals. Records are indexed by name, so a searcher looks up owners rather than addresses.

Does paying off a mortgage produce a new deed?

No. The lender files a satisfaction piece to show the loan is paid, and the original deed remains your proof of ownership. A copy of the deed can be bought through Landex or requested by email from the office.

Can documents be filed by mail or electronically?

Yes, with conditions. A mailed package needs original signatures, notary stamps and the exact fee. Electronic filing must come through ePN, CSC or Simplifile. Plans and notary filings need an appointment.

Westmoreland County by the numbers

How does the Westmoreland County recorder process a deed?

A cashier checks it, a barcode goes on every page, it is scanned, and the details are keyed into the index. The Recorder of Deeds in Greensburg describes those four steps on its own pages, and the whole routine is built for speed.

At the first step the cashier confirms that the paper is an original, properly signed, dated and acknowledged before a notary whose seal, signature and commission expiration date appear. Fees and transfer taxes are collected at that moment. Then a 15-digit number is assigned, and a sticker on each page shows the page count, the amount paid and the date and time of recording. After scanning, the document goes back to the person who filed it, in person or by mail. Data entry staff finish the index from the legal description, and a second team double-checks it.

The county says Westmoreland is one of only two counties in Pennsylvania where deeds are recorded and returned right away, with no wait of a day or two. That is useful to a seller, because the new owner's name reaches the public record on closing day. County offices keep normal hours of 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. on weekdays, and they close on the county holiday calendar.

The same office also runs a Veterans' Identification Discount Card program for veterans living in the county, announced on its main page, and it publishes a free guide to searching records by name, instrument number, document category, municipality, subdivision or lot. Searches by tax map number or UPI also work, though only where the original document listed one.

What does the Westmoreland County recorder charge?

A deed or a mortgage costs $110.25 to record. Every listed document includes four names, four pages, one tax map number and one UPI, and the office asks for exact payment with anything sent in.

Westmoreland County recording fees, from the county fee schedule
Document or itemFee
Deed$110.25
Mortgage$110.25

Mortgage satisfaction or release$84.25

Extra UPI$20.00

Questions about any charge go to 724-830-3518 or ROD@westmorelandcountypa.gov. Payment can be cash, money order, cashier's or certified check, or a personal check with ID. Debit and credit cards are not accepted. When you send several documents, the office will not take one check for more than five, so each document after the fifth needs its own.

What is the 10-digit PIN and why do Westmoreland deeds need one?

It is the parcel identifier number, and Westmoreland County requires it on every document it records. The county describes it as a 10-digit number, and the first digits point to the district, the map page and the lot, which the Tax Claim Bureau explains in its tax sale notes.

Getting the PIN right matters more than most sellers expect. A deed with a missing or wrong number is one of the quickest ways to have a closing package returned. If you cannot find the number on a tax bill, ask the Tax Assessment Office at 40 North Pennsylvania Avenue, Suite 440, Greensburg, or search the county's online record index. The index lets you search by name, by instrument number, or, for older records, by book and page for anything recorded before November 13, 2000.

Tax map numbers were not required until 2009, so documents from before then may not appear in a search by map number.

How do you e-record a deed in Westmoreland County?

Open an account with SimpliFile or CSC and upload the scanned original. Each vendor sets its own sign-up steps, and the county recommends reading them first.

Documents sent that way are first routed to the county's UPI and GIS Tax Mapping department for review, then forwarded to the recorder once certified. Nearly every document type can go this way, with one exception: anything that includes an attachment to the Statement of Value must come by mail or in person. The county explains the reason. An e-recorded attachment would add to the page count, and the office cannot alter the page count, so you would pay for pages that cost nothing when handed over the counter.

  • Stamped, self-addressed envelopes are required for mailed recordings and requests.
  • Include a phone number with your paperwork.
  • Plans must have original signatures, and the 18 by 24 inch plan fee is $49.00 for the first page and $20.00 for each page after that.

What transfer tax paperwork goes with a Westmoreland County deed?

Either the tax itself or a Statement of Value. Pennsylvania imposes a 1 percent state realty transfer tax, and the Department of Revenue says both buyer and seller are jointly liable. The county's recorder collects it, often alongside a local share.

The county's fee schedule says every deed has to state the true consideration or come with two copies of an Affidavit of Value. Any claimed exemption, whether full or partial, must be backed by that affidavit filed in duplicate, with street addresses, consideration, assessed value, fair market value, mortgages recorded and an explanation of why the transaction is or is not taxable. The affidavit must cite the regulation that supports the exemption.

  • Family transfers are the usual exemption, and the recording rules say the exemption must be clearly stated in the deed.
  • A deed with taxes in more than one municipality must say how the transfer taxes are divided.
  • The county publishes a Realty Transfer Tax Rates sheet; ask the office for it, since the rates differ by municipality.

What is Westmoreland County like for a house sale?

It is a Pittsburgh-area county of 1,036 square miles with 349,324 residents in the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate. QuickFacts reports 169,961 housing units, 154,979 households and a 78.4 percent owner-occupancy rate for 2020 to 2024.

The median value of an owner-occupied home is $203,500, median gross rent is $879, and median household income is $74,109. Owners with a mortgage have median monthly costs of $1,452. Population has slipped 1.5 percent since the 2020 census, from 354,663.

Greensburg is the county seat, and the county's other cities are Arnold, Jeannette, Latrobe, Lower Burrell, Monessen and New Kensington. Coal, coke, steel and glass built the county after the Civil War, and Volkswagen ran a plant near New Stanton from 1978 to 1988. The county's Land Bank and Development Authority work on vacant, abandoned and tax-delinquent properties, a reminder that older neighborhoods vary a great deal. Nineteen school districts serve the county, among them Greensburg-Salem, Hempfield Area, Norwin, Franklin Regional, Greater Latrobe and Penn-Trafford. Greensburg's January average is 28.7 degrees and its July average 71.8, so a house sees real winters.

More questions about Westmoreland County, PA Recorder of Deeds

How much does it cost to record a deed in Westmoreland County?

A deed costs $110.25, which includes four names, four pages, one tax map number and one UPI. Extra names cost $0.50, extra pages $2.00 and extra UPIs $20.00. Realty transfer tax is collected separately.

Does the Westmoreland County recorder take credit cards?

No. The payment policy lists cash, money orders, cashier's or certified checks and personal checks, and it states that debit and credit cards are not accepted. In person, a personal check needs a valid photo ID and the signer must be present.

Can I e-record every document in Westmoreland County?

Almost all of them. The one exception is a document with an attachment to the Statement of Value, which must be mailed or brought in. Use SimpliFile or CSC for everything else.

What happens if I send several documents in one envelope?

The office accepts one check for no more than five documents. Enclose a separate check for each document beyond the first five, plus a stamped, self-addressed return envelope.

Is a PIN required on a Westmoreland County deed?

Yes. Westmoreland County requires a 10-digit parcel identifier number on all documents, in addition to the usual acknowledgment and notary details. Ask the Tax Assessment Office if you cannot find it.

What we confirmed on the official page

  • Transfer taxes or Statement of Value must accompany deeds; state 1% + local 1% (Peters Township 1.5%); three separate checks required where transfer taxes due.

Fees

Selling in Washington County?
We buy Washington County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

What we could not confirm

  • No e-recording enrollment details found on official site

Washington County by the numbers

Where does a Washington County, PA deed get recorded?

At the Recorder of Deeds office in the Crossroads Center, 95 W. Beau St., Suite 520, Washington, PA 15301; the number is 724-228-6806. Staff are in from 9:00 a.m. until 4:30 p.m., though the 4:00 p.m. mark is the real deadline, because recording itself stops then.

The office dates from 1781, the year the county was cut out of Westmoreland County. By its own account it records deeds, mortgages, subdivision plans and other papers the state treats as permanent, collects the fees and taxes attached to them, and sends the receipts on to the state, the county, the municipalities and the school districts. Everything is indexed, verified and scanned the same business day.

A Washington County sale ends at this counter. The deed is signed at closing and then recorded here, which is the moment the buyer's name enters the public record. To see what is already on file against a property, search Landex, which holds every deed from 1781 to the present, or sit at one of the public computers in the office.

What does the Washington County recorder charge to record a deed?

The base fee depends on document type, and every base fee already covers four pages, four indexed names and one PIN. The county posts a fee schedule and a fee calculator on the recorder page, so check the current figure there before you write a check.

Washington County recorder charges on top of the base fee, from the county recorder page
ItemCharge
Included in the base fee4 pages, 4 indexed names, 1 PIN
Each additional page$2.00
Each additional indexed name$0.50
Each additional PIN$10.00
CJEA surcharge after the fiscal code changeUp from $2.50 to $3.50, a $1 increase

The county explains that the printed schedule lags behind the $1 CJEA increase, so a recent schedule on the site may show a figure $1 lower than what the counter collects. If the total is unclear, the office asks you to call 724-228-6806 rather than guess.

Two small details catch people out. The PIN charge applies per parcel number, so a sale that combines several parcels costs more than a single-lot sale. And the extra-page charge adds up on long documents, such as a deed that carries a full legal description and several exhibits.

Who pays realty transfer tax on a Washington County sale?

Both do, in the eyes of the state. The Pennsylvania Department of Revenue sets the commonwealth tax at 1 percent of the value transferred and makes grantor and grantee jointly and severally liable, so the state can pursue either party for the whole amount.

County recorders collect that share and usually a local share too, then pass the money along. Washington County's page lists the state, county, municipalities and school districts as the recipients, which means the local rate follows the municipality. Get the combined rate from the recorder or your closing agent before you settle on a net price.

  • Exempt transfers include some between relatives, some to government bodies, and property passing under a will or by intestacy.
  • An exemption claim normally needs paperwork, so ask the office which form goes with the deed.
  • Who bears the cost is a term of the sale contract, not something the recorder decides.

What formatting rules can get a Washington County document rejected?

Page size and type size are the two that the county stresses on its recorder page. The office no longer accepts legal-size pages electronically, and it sets minimum fonts: 12 point on letter-size pages and 14 point on legal-size pages.

Subdivision plans follow their own rules. They are filed on paper or mylar, and they need signatures from the Washington County Planning Commission, the local planning commission where one applies, the board of supervisors or borough council, and the owners of the land being divided. The plan also carries an engineer's seal, and it has to be recorded within 90 days of the local governing body's approval.

  • Check page size before you scan a deed for e-recording.
  • Confirm the type size on a long exhibit, since small print is a common reason for a bounce.
  • For a plan, count the 90 days from the local approval, not from the date you finish the drawings.

What is Washington County like for a house sale?

It is a large, mostly owner-occupied county south of Pittsburgh. QuickFacts credits it with 210,802 residents in 2025 on 857 square miles of land, plus 99,340 housing units and 88,505 households in the 2020 to 2024 survey.

About 76.1 percent of households own where they live. Owner-occupied homes have a median value of $228,500, rent runs a median $949, and the typical household earns $78,958. People with a mortgage pay a median $1,618 a month in housing costs.

Washington is the county seat and Monongahela the only other city. Canonsburg and Charleroi are two of the larger boroughs, and Peters Township is the biggest municipality. Washington & Jefferson College is in the city of Washington, coal mining continues at the Enlow Fork mine, and the Southpointe business park spreads over more than 800 acres. About 37.8 inches of snow fall in a typical year, mostly from November to April, so buyers touring an older house will look hard at the roof and the furnace.

Which school districts and towns shape buyer demand in Washington County?

Canon-McMillan, Peters Township, Charleroi, Burgettstown Area and Chartiers-Houston are among the districts that draw different groups of buyers. The county is split into many small districts, so neighbors on opposite sides of a boundary can pay different school taxes.

For that reason, a listing in Washington County sells better when it names the district. Peters Township is the largest municipality, and Charleroi is a river borough named after the Belgian city, because Belgian glassmakers settled the Monongahela area in the late 1800s. The countywide median home value of $228,500 hides a lot of variation, so look at recent sales inside the specific district.

What if the house has unpaid taxes before the deed is recorded?

Two county offices share the work. The Treasurer collects county taxes at 95 W. Beau St., Suite 130, 724-228-6780, with the counter open 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. The Tax Revenue Department, in Suite 525 at 724-228-6850, handles both assessments and delinquent claims.

Since October 6, 2025 the Treasurer has refused personal checks for delinquent taxes. Certified checks, money orders, cash and cards are accepted. Paying online adds a charge: 2.50 percent with a $2.00 minimum on cards, or $1.50 for an electronic check.

When back taxes are attached to the house you plan to sell, request a written balance from Tax Revenue ahead of closing so your closing agent can settle it from the proceeds. Washington County also has a Board of Assessment Appeals, and Tax Revenue can describe the filing steps.

More questions about Washington County, PA Recorder of Deeds

What time does the Washington County recorder stop accepting deeds?

Recording ends at 4:00 p.m., half an hour before the office closes. The address is 95 W. Beau St., Suite 520, Washington. A deed that shows up after 4:00 p.m. is held for the next business day.

Can I record a legal-size deed electronically in Washington County?

No. The county says it no longer accepts legal-size pages electronically. Letter-size pages need at least 12 point type and legal-size pages need at least 14 point, so bring a paper original if the document is on legal paper.

Does a Washington County deed fee cover extra pages and names?

The base fee covers four pages, four indexed names and one PIN. Each page beyond four costs $2.00, each extra name $0.50 and each extra PIN $10.00, and the county added $1 to its CJEA surcharge, so confirm the total by phone at 724-228-6806.

How can I look up recorded deeds in Washington County, PA?

Use Landex online, which holds deeds from 1781 to the present, or use the public computers inside the Recorder of Deeds office. Landex support is 1-800-370-2836, option 4, according to the county page.

Who owes the transfer tax when a Washington County house sells?

Both sides are liable. Pennsylvania charges 1 percent of the value transferred and holds buyer and seller jointly responsible, and a local tax normally rides along. The sale contract decides who pays in practice; the recorder can confirm the local rate.

Erie County by the numbers

Where is the Erie County Recorder of Deeds?

The Recorder of Deeds is a division of the Erie County Clerk of Records, and it sits in Room 121 of Erie County Courthouse I, 140 W. Sixth Street, Erie, PA 16501. The phone number is 814-451-6246, the fax is 814-451-6213, and the office takes email at recorder@eriecountypa.gov.

Its main job is to review, record and index documents that relate to Erie County real estate and to give the public and real estate professionals access to those records. Between 100 and 400 documents come through each day, so a deed with a missing page or a wrong fee can sit in a pile of returns.

The office acts as collection agent for the county, the Pennsylvania Department of Revenue, the Department of State, and the municipalities and school districts inside the county line. It does not run on county tax dollars, and the county says it brings in more revenue than it spends. Staff cannot give legal advice on your deed, so route questions about wording to a lawyer or your title company.

How much does it cost to record a deed in Erie County?

The base fee for an Erie County deed is $87.00 under the schedule effective December 1, 2025. Mortgages and a few other conveyance-type papers carry the same base fee, while smaller instruments cost less.

InstrumentBase fee
Deed, mortgage, excerpt of adjudication, declaration of acquisition$87.00
Mortgage satisfaction, assignment or release$59.75
Easement, right of way, land contract$59.75

Lease under 30 years, agreement exempt from transfer tax, all other instruments$18.50

Add-ons apply when a document is bigger than the base allows.

  • Indexed names over four: $0.50 each
  • Pages over four: $2.00 each
  • Additional parcels: $0.50 each
  • Statement of Value: $2.00
  • Copies picked up, emailed or faxed: $0.25 per page
  • Certification: $1.00 per document

Each amount carries an asterisk on the schedule, so confirm the final total with the office before a closing check is cut.

Does Erie County charge transfer tax on a home sale?

Yes. The office collects Pennsylvania and local realty transfer tax on all realty transfers and sends the money to the Commonwealth and to the municipality or school district. The county points to 72 P.S. Section 8101-C and following, and 61 Pa. Code Section 91.101 and following, as the governing rules.

Some transfers are exempt. The county gives transactions between husband and wife, between parent and child, and between siblings as examples. Do not assume a family sale qualifies. The claim is made on the Statement of Value form, and the recorder reviews what the paper shows.

  • The Statement of Value costs $2.00 to record.
  • The Common Level Ratio printed on the 2025 schedule was 1.88 for July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026.
  • The local rate depends on the municipality, so ask the office for the rate in your township, borough or city.

The 1.88 figure covers a fiscal year that has ended. Ask the recorder which factor applies to a document dated after June 30, 2026.

How do you look up Erie County deeds and get copies?

The Recorder posts an online index and images through Infocon, at www.infoconcountyaccess.com. The office also lists an E-Recording information page for title companies and other filers.

Because a fire destroyed the Erie County Courthouse on March 23, 1823, records accumulated before that date were lost. Researchers tracing a very old chain of title should expect gaps and should ask the office what survives.

Mail documents to Recorder of Deeds, 140 West 6th Street, Room 121, Erie, PA 16501. Include the right fees and a Statement of Value if one is needed, and put a return address on the package so the recorded deed finds its way back to you.

What would a typical Erie County deed cost to record?

A six-page deed with six indexed names and a Statement of Value comes to $94.00 before transfer tax. That is the $87.00 base, $4.00 for two extra pages, $1.00 for two extra names and $2.00 for the Statement of Value. The asterisk on the schedule means the office should confirm the total, so treat this as a planning figure.

The recording fee is small next to the tax. Erie County's base is $87.00, while a four-page deed in Delaware County runs $117.25 and in Elk County $92.75, so Erie County sits in the middle of these three. The larger cost in any sale is the realty transfer tax, which scales with the price rather than the page count.

On a $177,000 sale, the median owner-occupied value in the county, the 1% state share alone is $1,770 before the local share is added. The seller and buyer split that bill according to the sales agreement.

What other fees does the Erie County office list?

The schedule includes several items that come up around a sale. A notary appointment or renewal is $30.50 plus a $3.50 prothonotary fee. A storm water management map, planned community map or condominium plan is $30.00, the same as a subdivision map.

The county collects low-income housing fees and record management fees along with Erie County recording fees and the Pennsylvania writ tax. All fees and taxes are set by Pennsylvania law or local ordinance, so the recorder cannot negotiate them.

What is Erie County like for a home seller?

Erie County is the northernmost county in Pennsylvania. It has 1,558 square miles of total area, but 49% of that is water, because Lake Erie borders it to the north. It is the only county in the state that borders New York, Ohio and Canada across the lake.

Erie County has two cities, Erie and Corry, plus Millcreek, Harborcreek, Summit and Fairview townships and boroughs such as Edinboro, North East, Girard, Waterford and Union City. The county was created in 1800 and organized in 1803.

Settlement came late. The federal government resolved the competing New York and Pennsylvania claims to the Erie Triangle in 1792, which let Pennsylvania buy the land, and the state created the county from part of Allegheny County on March 12, 1800. For its first years Erie County shared a temporary five-county administrative unit, based in Meadville, with Crawford, Mercer, Venango and Warren Counties. Its first local officials were elected in 1803.

  • North: Lake Erie
  • Northeast: Chautauqua County, New York
  • East: Warren County
  • South: Crawford County
  • West: Ashtabula County, Ohio

The Census Bureau counted 265,832 residents in its July 2025 estimate, a 1.9% drop from the April 2020 base, and 120,762 housing units. The median home value for 2020 to 2024 is $177,000. Downtown Erie averages 26.4 degrees in January and 70.8 in July, and Corry, inland, runs a little cooler, at 23.8 degrees in January and 68.2 in July.

More questions about Erie County, PA Recorder of Deeds

What is the base fee to record a deed in Erie County?

The base fee is $87.00 under the schedule effective December 1, 2025. Pages over four are $2.00 each and indexed names over four are $0.50 each.

Where do I send a deed for recording in Erie County?

Send it to Recorder of Deeds, 140 West 6th Street, Room 121, Erie, PA 16501. The office phone is 814-451-6246.

Are family transfers exempt from Erie County transfer tax?

Some are. The county names transactions between husband and wife, parent and child, and siblings as examples of exempt transfers, and the Statement of Value is how the exemption is claimed.

How much does a Statement of Value cost in Erie County?

It costs $2.00 on the current schedule. Additional parcels are $0.50 each.

Can I search Erie County deeds online?

Yes. The office offers an online index and images through Infocon at www.infoconcountyaccess.com. Copies picked up or emailed are $0.25 per page.

Beaver County by the numbers

What does the Beaver County Recorder of Deeds do?

The office files the deeds, mortgages and related papers that make a property sale part of the public record in Beaver County. It sits in the Third Street section on the first floor of the Beaver County Courthouse at 810 Third Street in Beaver, and the phone is 724-770-4560. Counter hours run 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Monday through Friday.

Recording in Beaver County started in 1800, the year the county was created, and every record has since been digitized. Besides deeds and mortgages, the office takes sheriff deeds, tax claim deeds, satisfactions, assignments, releases, restrictive covenants, leases, installment land contracts, Clean and Green filings and notary bonds. It also collects the Pennsylvania realty transfer tax and passes the local share to the municipality and school district.

If you own a house here, the office offers a free Fraud Alert sign-up that sends a notice whenever a deed or mortgage is recorded under your name. Others in the county may share your name, so check any alert against your own property before reacting.

Where is Beaver County, and who sells a house there?

Beaver County sits in the Greater Pittsburgh region, was formed on March 12, 1800 from parts of Allegheny and Washington counties, and takes its name from the Beaver River. It covers 444 square miles, about 9 of them water. The Ohio River cuts through the county and separates the southern third from the northern two thirds, and Beaver is the county seat while Aliquippa is the largest city. Beaver Falls is the county's other city, and the rest of the map is boroughs and townships.

Census QuickFacts puts the 2025 population estimate at 166,032, a drop of 1.3% from the 2020 base. The county counts 79,845 housing units and 72,257 households, and 75.0% of homes are owner-occupied. For owner-occupied homes the median value in 2020 to 2024 was $190,900, and median gross rent was $890. Residents 65 and older make up 24.8% of the population, which is why many sales here follow an estate or a move to smaller housing.

Getting around is easy for a buyer who commutes. The Pennsylvania Turnpike, I-376 and US 30 all cross the county, along with a long list of state routes. Climate is the hot-summer humid continental type, with January averages near 29 degrees and July near 73 in the Beaver and Rochester area.

How much transfer tax is due on a Beaver County sale?

The total is 2% of the value being conveyed: 1% to the state and 1% to local governments, split evenly between the municipality and the school district. The county notes that this value is not always the sales price. The Recorder collects all of it at the time of recording and will not accept a deed until the tax is paid.

The state and local governments do not care who pays, so the purchase agreement decides. On most agreements the buyer and seller split it, but the new owner answers for any shortfall if the amount is later questioned. Recording fees and both taxes can go on one check made payable to the Recorder of Deeds, and the office takes only cash or check.

Beaver County transfer tax parts and copy charges, per the Recorder's Taxes and FAQ pages
ItemAmount
State realty transfer tax1% of value
Municipal share0.5% of value
School district share0.5% of value
Copy made at the counter$1.00 per page
Copy by mail$5 flat plus $1.00 per page
Certification of a copy$1.50

The recording fee for a deed changed on December 1, 2025, when a new fee schedule took effect that includes a $1 Criminal Justice Enhancement Account charge under Act 45 of 2025. Ask the Recorder's office for the current schedule before you budget for closing.

What is a statement of value, and what is the common level ratio?

A statement of value is a state form, filed in duplicate, that either sets the value of the property or states the reason a transfer is exempt. The office requires one whenever the tax is not paid or the deed does not show the true value, such as a deed reciting $1.00 of consideration. State investigators can review those filings later.

Completing the form needs the common level ratio for Beaver County. The State Tax Equalization Board set the factor at 1.34, and it applies to documents accepted from July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027. Under 61 Pa. Code 91.02, the date of acceptance is presumed to be the date of execution written in the deed.

  • Exempt transfers named by the county include those between spouses, parent and child, grandparent and grandchild, siblings, and a stepparent and stepchild.
  • Other exemptions exist for particular situations, and the county points owners to an attorney or the Pennsylvania Department of Revenue.
  • If the state later decides the value was higher, or an exemption does not hold, the Department of Revenue mails a determination. You pay the added state and local tax plus interest to the state, and the Recorder then disburses the local share.

How do you record a deed in Beaver County?

You can bring it to the courthouse or send it by mail. In person, the office says review, receipt and scanning usually take 10 to 15 minutes, and the recorded original is mailed back within about a week. If a mailed package has not arrived after two weeks, the county suggests contacting the Postal Service.

Mailed packages need a check payable to the Recorder of Deeds for the right amount and a self-addressed stamped envelope with enough postage. The office takes no responsibility for postage that falls short or for returns lost by the Postal Service, and the FAQ advises against mailing cash. Most sellers never handle this step, because the title company or closing attorney files the deed. Ask whoever is running your closing to confirm the filing date and send you the recorded copy.

  • Documents that touch more than one municipality need the local tax split clearly stated.
  • Subdivision plans must be 18 by 24 inches or 24 by 36 inches, original on linen or mylar, and cannot be older than 90 days from governing body approval.
  • A veteran's discharge can be recorded through the Veterans Office in the courthouse basement, and the Recorder issues certified copies at no charge.

How do you look up a deed or a mortgage in Beaver County?

Beaver County indexes by name, not by street address or tax parcel number. To find a deed or mortgage you need the name of the grantor, grantee, mortgagor or mortgagee and the approximate year. Parcel numbers come from the Assessment Office, so a seller who only has an address should start there.

Every document in the office is public except military discharge papers, which are impounded. Staff can answer general questions by phone but are not permitted to run searches or give legal advice, so a title searcher or attorney handles anything deeper. To trace ownership backward, read the recital that follows the legal description, usually beginning with the word Being, and follow it through each prior deed toward 1800.

The county records deeds for land only, not buildings. Older deeds sometimes mention when a structure was built, and the price of a conveyance can hint at it, but the Recorder does not keep construction records. Check with the municipality for those.

What should a Beaver County seller do about liens and mortgage satisfactions?

Confirm that the payoff of your existing mortgage ends with a recorded satisfaction piece. The lender starts that step, and it may send you the forms. If it fails to file, you can bring or mail the original satisfaction piece to the Recorder with the fee on the current schedule and a stamped return envelope.

Before you list, pull your own name from the index and read what is recorded against it. Open mortgages, old easements and agreements show up there, and clearing a missing satisfaction is quicker before an offer than during the closing window.

  • Gather the last recorded deed and its recital.
  • Ask the Assessment Office for the parcel number.
  • Ask your lender for the recorded satisfaction on any paid-off loan.
  • Agree in writing who pays the 2% transfer tax.

More questions about Beaver County, PA Recorder of Deeds

Who pays the realty transfer tax when a house sells in Beaver County?

The contract decides, and the county's offices do not mind which side pays as long as the full amount is collected at recording. On most agreements the buyer and seller split it, but the new owner is responsible if the amount is questioned later.

What hours is the Beaver County Recorder of Deeds open?

The office is open 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Monday through Friday, at 810 Third Street in Beaver. The phone number is 724-770-4560, and it is on the first floor of the courthouse in the Third Street section.

Can I pay the recording fee and transfer tax with one check?

Yes. Recording fees plus the state and local taxes can all be on one check made payable to the Recorder of Deeds. The office accepts only cash or check, and it asks you not to mail cash.

Does the Recorder search by address in Beaver County?

No. The indexes are by the names of grantor, grantee, mortgagor and mortgagee, grouped by year. Parcel numbers and addresses are handled by the Assessment Office.

How long does Beaver County take to return a recorded deed?

A walk-in filing is reviewed, receipted and scanned in about 10 to 15 minutes, and the recorded original is mailed back within about a week. If a mailed filing has not come back after two weeks, contact the Postal Service.

Butler County by the numbers

Where is a Butler County deed filed?

Butler County deeds are recorded at the Recorder of Deeds office in the Government Center, Floor L, 124 West Diamond Street, Butler, PA 16001. The mailing address is P.O. Box 1208, Butler, PA 16003, and the office phone is 724-284-5340. Online, the county runs a deed search and a fee schedule on its Recorder of Deeds pages.

The county also posts a cover date that shows how far recordings have been verified. When that date trails the day you recorded, an index search will not yet show your deed, so check it before telling a buyer the record is clean. Plan books for subdivisions are posted online starting at Plan Book 315, page 27.

What are the Butler County recording fees?

The base fee for a deed, a mortgage or a re-recorded deed is $87.75 for four names, four pages and one parcel, a rate that began on November 19, 2025. Extras are small: $1 for each name beyond four, $2 for each page beyond four and $0.50 for each parcel beyond the first.

Butler County Recorder base fees from the county's fee pages, effective November 19, 2025
DocumentBase fee
Deed, mortgage or re-recording of a deed$87.75
Re-recording of a mortgage$89.75
